query: Side Bets {You find a place on the cellar steps. The bookmaker works his way along them, slate in hand.|From the steps you can see the fighters' wand hands, which tell you more than their faces. The bookmaker is coming round.|You know the regulars on the steps now, and who bets with their heart. The bookmaker holds out his slate.} Back the favourite {Your fighter wins. You collect quietly and leave before anyone remembers your face.|You read the wand hands right. The bookmaker pays you as if it hurt.|The favourite wins, as favourites do. You pocket a small, sensible profit.} {Your fighter goes down in the first exchange. So does your stake.|You picked the wand hand, not the wizard. The bookmaker smiles.|The favourite slips on the wet stone, and your crowns slip with them.} Back the underdog {The underdog wins, and you're the only one on the steps who backed them. The bookmaker counts it out very slowly.|Your long shot lands one spell, and it's enough. The steps turn round to look at you.|You saw what nobody else did, the limp in the favourite's step. You walk home heavy with silver.} {The underdog is an underdog for a reason. Your stake is gone in a minute.|A brave fight, a long fall, and your crowns go with it.|You backed your heart. Your purse pays for it.} Go home {You watch one bout and go home with your purse unopened.|You leave before the bookmaker reaches you.|You climb the steps into the cold and leave the ring to its noise.}
